newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end off, look to U.S. for clues.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end off, look to U.S. for clues.

text.p: Austrian shares trailed Germany and the United States lower on Friday, ending 1.18 percent down, and traders said they were watching to see whether the ATX index would hold onto 1,100 points in the coming week.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 13.26 points down at 1,108.64, with 19 issues down and two up. Market participants saw solid support for the ATX index at 1,080.
"The 1,100 points level has a psychological significance but the market could slide towards 1,080 if Wall Street continues to fall," a trader said.
Among the biggest decliners were luxiery hosiery maker Wolford and preferential shares in Creditanstalt-Bankverein.
Wolford, which presents its half-year results on Monday, slumped 7.27 percent to 1,136 schillings.
Creditanstalt preferred dipped 5.37 percent to 494.90 schillings. The long-awaited privatisation of the bank has entered a new phase of uncertainty.
Brewer Brau Union and fibre maker Lenzing were the only gainers. Brau Union advanced 0.77 percent to 654 schillings on relatively low volume of 3,729 lots.
December ATX futures stood 14.8 points down at 1,102.2.
The borad-based Vienna Bourse index eased 3.83 points at 419.87 -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
